title: Slices
description: Dynamic slices in Go - like arrays but growable
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Spans and ranges

Rust slices map well to **`ReadOnlySpan<T>`** and **range syntax** (`arr[1..^1]`).

exercises.title: Create Slice
exercises.description: Create a slice with make for 3 ints. Assign values 1,2,3. Print using Console.WriteLine.
exercises.starter_code:
var s = new int[3];
// assign 1,2,3 and print

exercises.title: Append to Slice
exercises.description: Create slice nums := []int{1, 2}. Append 3, 4, 5. Print result.

exercises.title: Slice Length and Capacity
exercises.description: Create slice s := make([]int, 3, 10). Print its len and cap.

exercises.title: Slice Literals
exercises.description: Create slice fruits := []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}. Print its length.

exercises.title: Slicing a Slice
exercises.description: Create slice n := []int{1,2,3,4,5}. Slice it to get [2,3,4] (elements at index 1,2,3). Print result.
hints: Use n[1:4] to get elements from index 1 to 3

exercises.title: Append Slices
exercises.description: Create two slices: a := []int{1, 2} and b := []int{3, 4, 5}. Append all elements of b to a and print the result.
hints: Use append(a, b...) to append all elements of slice b to a
The ... expands the slice into individual arguments

exercises.title: Copy Slice
exercises.description: Create slice original := []int{1, 2, 3}. Make an independent copy and append 4 to the copy. Print both.
exercises.starter_code:
var original = new[] { 1, 2, 3 };
// copy, append 4, print both
